## Key Research Highlights & Spec Commentary



**_AMKR: Near-Term Trajectory Tempered on Softer Comms/Consumer, But Long-Term
AI Packaging Thesis
Intact._******[Here](https://jpmorgan.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14287469&ad=5063781598&h=_dxBkjS&sig=4EFAFhpe2sv2QrQOvotGc0VTqjo&v=2&isig=JNE8OBvE3BmW1iNUjYHuJC3hvso&url=https://markets.jpmorgan.com/research/email/scx/-nhhkoh7/GPS-5504968-0.pdf/b7f17878-d658-4041-9d9e-de26ed0e58cf)  
Mayur Ramdhani flags **a softer setup for AMKR** despite record Computing and
Auto/Industrial revenue for a second straight quarter and continued GM
expansion (+150bps to 18.3%). The **Dec-Q guide of $1.9-2b came in below
Street** _on broadening Comms (SiP migration to Vietnam, component shortages)
and Consumer weakness (mid-teens% QoQ decline)_ – likely weaker Apple/QCOM
momentum and supply constraints - which he views as **a 1-2 quarter blip
rather than structural**. Computing remains the key bull case lever, guided up
low-double-digits QoQ (>50% YoY) on the flagship HDFO CPU (Vera) ramp, an
additional hyperscaler HDFO program (likely MSFT Cobalt), and two 2.5D
networking/switch programs (likely Tomahawk 6 & an NVDA switch IC), though the
ramp cadence is proving less linear than the prior "+30% QoQ" framing. The
bigger swing factor is capex, with CY27 facilities-only spend now >$2b
(Arizona ~$1.8b) and CY28-29 peaking as Phase 1 ramp overlaps Phase 2
construction — but Mayur argues the funding profile is better than it looks
given likely CHIPS Act 48D ITC coverage, ~$3b of NVDA prepayments expected in
CY27, and ~$500m of customer prepayments already on balance sheet across a
12-customer framework. Mayur lowers CY26/CY27 EPS estimates (2.52/2.89, down
from 2.73/3.47) but keeps the Dec-27 PT unchanged, viewing AMKR's long-term AI
advanced packaging and geopolitical-alternative positioning as intact.

_In Asia,[Gokul’s
takeaway](https://jpmorgan.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14287469&ad=5063781598&h=Y8YaaM4&sig=EvLN6E8BL9dhqGYUpU8aImmLx4a&v=2&isig=3YnzlACFLvRylBldnuZqpl5ANQc&url=https://markets.jpmorgan.com/research/email/scx/1r73hc7b/GPS-5509389-0.pdf/b7f17878-d658-4041-9d9e-de26ed0e58cf)
is that the OSAT pricing environment continues to look favorable, given strong
demand, tight capacity, and cost pass-through. Given the smooth ramp of ASE's
first full-process project (AMD Venice CPU, in our view), he believes that ASE
is likely to break into NVDA Vera as a second source, with the potential to
support AWS Trainium 3 in the coming year. _

**_  _**

**_CDNS | Strong Print & Guide on Record Backlog; Agentic AI Proof Points Challenge LLM Fears._** [Here](https://jpmorgan.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14287469&ad=5063781598&h=qAmt8MX&sig=Qt9seZgfBLQYwAEH0xlgOPwO0tT&v=2&isig=8b9b3Ha07gKOz6zYTuUhVmG9n4n&url=https://markets.jpmorgan.com/research/email/scx/5sva61ih/GPS-5508302-0.pdf/b7f17878-d658-4041-9d9e-de26ed0e58cf)  
 _Last night I shared[my first take
(here)](https://jpmorgan.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14287469&ad=5063781598&h=cAl3HfV&sig=Yg7veNjlCXKH6zOZO81qb7rTLRA&v=2&isig=5FdjuYx3VjMvUMbtrttqCbCEiGa&url=https://markets.jpmorgan.com/research/email/scx/-mv6b92g/GPS-5508624-0/b7f17878-d658-4041-9d9e-de26ed0e58cf)
on CDNS’ solid print and nicely better-than-expected guide. Investor feedback
was similarly quite positive – impressed with the growing backlog and pleased
with the company’s answers to questions about AI opportunities, hardware
growth, and some small timing issues. _This morning **Harlan Sur weighs in on
the clean 3Q26 beat-and-raise** , underscoring +22%YoY revenue growth and EPS
beating the high end of guidance, as well as a **record backlog of $8.2b**
(the fifth straight quarter of growth – a bit below Bloomberg consensus, but
the sample was small), with double-digit growth across core EDA (+20%), IP
(+24%), and SD&A (+30%). The team raised FY26 guidance, getting to ~$8.40 in
EPS, with YTD bookings up 26% and recurring revenue growth accelerating to
+18%YoY. The key product announcement was Maestro, CDNS' new semiconductor-
specific AI model family (30% better quality, 5x token efficiency vs. general
foundation models), with **active AI agent engagements scaling** to 100+ (from
45+ last quarter), reinforcing the thesis that __agentic AI is driving
incremental - not cannibalistic - EDA usage__. Capital returns also increased,
with the buyback doubled to $400m/quarter and a $2.5b authorization add.
Harlan raises CY26/CY27 EPS +4%/+8% and with it his 43x F27 PER-derived TP +4%
to $420.

**_  _**

**_CLS | 3Q26 Quick-take – ’27 Outlook Raises the Bar, bug FCF Questions Linger._** [Here](https://jpmorgan.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14287469&ad=5063781598&h=20Ueb56&sig=VXKIMrkS5imDLgGDPkmaCUk42Nj&v=2&isig=OWNgWvbQnrRH4ys5SRd81uiCJG8&url=https://markets.jpmorgan.com/research/email/scx/53vundqf/GPS-5507742-0.pdf/b7f17878-d658-4041-9d9e-de26ed0e58cf)  
 _Last night I shared[my first take
(here)](https://jpmorgan.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14287469&ad=5063781598&h=cAl3HfV&sig=Yg7veNjlCXKH6zOZO81qb7rTLRA&v=2&isig=5FdjuYx3VjMvUMbtrttqCbCEiGa&url=https://markets.jpmorgan.com/research/email/scx/-mv6b92g/GPS-5508624-0/b7f17878-d658-4041-9d9e-de26ed0e58cf)
on CLS’ impressive print, crowned by a strong guide – including a bullish
first comment on ’28 (“customer demand forecasts meaningfully higher for
2028”). _Joe recaps the strong F3Q (high end of the guidance range) driven by
“strong Compute & Storage demand.” Though the 4Q guide was more mixed (revenue
tracked below his expectations) – and the team lowered ’26 FCF guidance -23%
to $460m – the ’27 revenue & OPM guides are well ahead of what Joe (and
consensus) expected; and he highlights the same bullish ’28 commentary. FCF
remains an area of focus for Joe on the call, though most investors I spoke
with seemed satisfied with the capex number. The call starts at 8am ET today.

_  _

_In Taiwan, Megan Hsueh provides[an update on liquid cooling project delays at
**AWS**](https://jpmorgan.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14287469&ad=5063781598&h=Huz19Nz&sig=eHCM2Xdch2gbAXIWw7cR0SQoGv&v=2&isig=TSW4RRuZaF6lgpkLzmw6Xs8Relq&url=https://markets.jpmorgan.com/research/email/scx/njfi6o30/GPS-5506491-0/b7f17878-d658-4041-9d9e-de26ed0e58cf),
where earlier this month he already warned of a two-month **delay in the
liquid-cooled T3 project** due to “hiccups in the downstream ramp.” He expects
this to be only a short-term product transition period, not requiring any
redesigns. As for **NVDA VR200** and **GOOGL TPU v8** ramps, they also saw
small delays, but are starting to ship now. VR200 volumes, though, look lower
than Albert initially expected, due to sub-optimal yields (“VR200 cold plate
shipments are now expected at **5–10k racks and ODM build at 5–7k** , versus
prior expectations of **> 10k**, due to sub-optimal downstream yields”). _

**Well, so much for easing into the week.** We’ve hardly even gotten to the
meat of earnings this week and somehow we already have a full plate. Elon
spent the weekend talking neocloud consolidation, the frontier world is
getting plenty of extra attention this morning, and META casually dropped a
$95B equity issuance into the mix. Never a dull moment. **On META, I’d view
the financing as a clearing event, both in terms of timing and the size of the
ask.** We weren’t expecting much more clarity until early 2027 anyway, so
getting it out of the way now removes one overhang earlier than expected. And
while $95B is obviously a big number, it’s arguably more digestible after all
the recent talk of potentially **“hundreds of billions”** of fundraising
following last week’s proxy. That said, flows are much more mixed today and
probably safe to buckle up for a choppy couple of days from here.



And we’re only getting started. Lots more to come this week, so **below are
the key incomings from this morning alongside the earnings lineup ahead**. As
always, here to catch up on any/all of it if helpful. CD



**KEY INCOMINGS******

  * **META****:** Officially raising $95B of equity, consisting of a $35B common/preferred offering and a $60B ATM program in new non-voting Class C shares, expected in Q1. The company also reiterated its 2026 capex targets. While we still need more clarity on 2027 spending, getting the financing out of the way earlier than the January timing expected last week is a positive and removes some overhang. This should serve as a modest clearing event, particularly after last week’s speculation around potentially “hundreds of billions” of fundraising. Flows are mixed so far, and we’d expect trading to remain choppy over the next two days.****

**  **

    * **SMID Ads** : By FAR the biggest question of the morning as SNAP, PINS, MGNI all down with no real headline/3p data to pin it to. Most rational explanation per feedback this morning seems to be that they’re getting used as funding shorts for META… sure...could be partly Brazil-driven too alongside one of my sellside peers cutting #s but still… yikes. ****

**  **

  * **VZ:** Feedback isn’t exactly warm, though I’d chalk a good chunk of this morning’s move up to the MVNO commentary on the call. It was a pretty hard pivot from the [rumors making the rounds Friday](https://x.com/OracleNYSE/status/2113640565468520795) and helped VZ outperform peers so not shocked to see the reversal. Schulman was pretty fired up on Starlink, making it crystal clear VZ is NOT doing an MVNO. He also pointed to the hurdles SpaceX still has to clear, though if/when they do, VZ plans to be “ferociously competitive.” So much for that. Stepping back, the numbers were solid, though bears are still relentlessly poking at the same old nits, particularly as to how much of the growth is really organic vs. Frontier/inorganic/cost cutting…and what happens in 2027 when those tailwinds start turning into headwinds. For read-throughs, FWA was probably the most interesting update from the call as VZ plans to launch 1Gbps FWA and add another 10–15M homes over the medium term. Hard to spin that as a positive for TMUS or Cable looking forward though near term I don’t think it should change the set-up (TMUS set-up below). Towers, meanwhile, could actually come out a winner, with VZ still having more mmWave buildout ahead.



  * **SEMIS** : Really interesting nugget from Tim Arcuri this morning, assessing his framework for what he believes is being implied by the semis stocks post this pullback. Remember he estimates that the supply chain is implying ~50GW of compute shipments in C2027 and ~70GW in C2028 and based on his math below, the recent move would imply something in the 50-52GW range - in other words, a cut of ~18-20GW vs his 70GW estimate [Link to note](https://analytics.ubs.com/b/ss/ubsextern-cca-prod/4/REDIR/?v5=Click&v6=SMEP&pe=lnk_o&pev2=link&events=event3&url=https%3A%2F%2Fneo.ubs.com%2Fshared%2Fd2lQhZ7Kfw&v2=4829&v3=1f1d1577bcc16bd0b742ae68c894f631~4095~822640653162042&v4=false&c3=1f1d1577bcc16bd0b742ae68c894f631~4095~822640653162042)

![](https://www.ubs.com/emas/CCA/f398badb-2d13-441f-af6a-5b3a9de7abcc/5fc27a89-4765-4115-ae28-023ed4b98b42.png)



**WHAT’S ON TAP?******

**  **

  * **AMT (10/27)** Generally speaking, towers are finally getting another look, with SpaceX’s purchase of low-band spectrum and as of Thursday night company looking for 80K cell sites across the US. While Starlink would likely lean heavily on terminals, femtocells and small cells, clearly they would need macro towers for broad urban/suburban coverage. As [Batya Levi pointed out in her preview](https://analytics.ubs.com/b/ss/ubsextern-cca-prod/4/REDIR/?v5=Click&v6=SMEP&pe=lnk_o&pev2=link&events=event3&url=https%3A%2F%2Furldefense.com%2Fv3%2F__https%3A%2Fanalytics.ubs.com%2Fb%2Fss%2Fubsextern-cca-prod%2F4%2FREDIR%2F%3Fv5%3DClick%26v6%3DSMEP%26pe%3Dlnk_o%26pev2%3Dlink%26events%3Devent3%26url%3Dhttps*3A*2F*2Fneo.ubs.com*2Fshared*2Fd2q3zKX8b4gFDK%26v2%3D4828%26v3%3D1f1d085062516f80aef03ecfd94c9266*2399*732121767952420%26v4%3Dfalse%26c3%3D1f1d085062516f80aef03ecfd94c9266*2399*732121767952420__%3BJSUlJSV-fn5-%21%21AHh8_Z5O2w%21n2dYBqFpA6RgOKwgVn62CFTzRqa4PgqCAnVBW-4HlVK-c7vBPk1IxzMx4u41RzqeyQ8zZnpnud8r-8rG4zkbCig--BH2c7fbvQ%24&v2=4829&v3=1f1d1577bcc16bd0b742ae68c894f631~4095~822640653258906&v4=false&c3=1f1d1577bcc16bd0b742ae68c894f631~4095~822640653258906), Echostar would be a useful comp as its buildout added **~3% to site rental revenues and 5-10%+ to AFFO/share** across the tower names. There may also be an opportunity for SpaceX to acquire Echostar’s existing spectrum-compatible equipment, helping it move faster. All said, Batya’s preference remains AMT > CCI > SBAC. On numbers, Batya believes AMT is tracking towards the high-end of its guidance range driven by stable US trends, solid growth internationally despite the Latam drag and robust growth at CoreSite. We expect the sale of its Canadian assets to have minimal impact on estimates.

** **

  * **GOOGL (10/28):** **Still feels like the consensus funding short across megacaps** , with search cannibalization fears getting louder, especially after META’s strength in ads. The AI strategy isn’t getting a free pass either following the latest Gemini delay and the days of GOOGL being a direct competitor to the leading frontier players now long gone.**** There’s been progress, particularly around Gemini 4 Argon, sure and the magnitude of TPU opportunity is very nascent, but investors still seem to want two things: a credible AI agent to help quiet the Muse/search fears and a broader Gemini 4 rollout before sentiment can really inflect to the upside again.

details / color; 3) GCP backlog conversion (any breadcrumbs around TPU margins
or QoQ $ trajectory), 4) Brand and direct response performance with thoughts
on consumer behavior, 5) impact of AI features on Search

**LO POSITIONING = OVERWEIGHT **(biased to downside)****

  * **EBAY (10/28)****Very debated name, although faster-money sentiment seems to lean pretty short**. Yes, GMV growth continues to show solid momentum per 3p data, led by collectibles, fashion, live, and other focus categories, though the bigger question, though, is whether the core marketplace is actually getting structurally healthier or if eBay is simply benefiting from a particularly strong collectibles cycle and whether Live is really as incremental to GMV as bulls currently believe (vs cannibalizing the core business). At the same time, this has quietly been one of the best-performing internet stocks YTD, up ~40%. The company also came out of the Muse mania earlier this fall relatively unscathed and largely avoided getting lumped into the broader consumer-friction basket, which feels somewhat fair given how niche much of its inventory is. That said, there are growing questions around whether EBAY is really as insulated from agents as the stock price suggests, particularly given its higher ad penetration and the FB Marketplace angle. The other major bear concern is heavier S&M spend in response to competitive pressure from Vinted. Bears remain skeptical that EPS growth can continue at the same pace and will be looking for any downward directional color on the 2027 OI outlook this quarter, although there’s no guarantee management actually provides it.

    * **3Q GMV** : +14-15% vs guide 10-12% FXN
    * **3Q OM:** lower end of guide 25.1-25.6% 
    * **4Q GMV Guide:** +10-12% FXN
    * **4Q OM Guide** : 25-25.5% 
    * **F27 OM** : directional commentary guiding down YoY vs street flat (NOT a given we get this)

**WHAT TO LISTEN FOR:** 1)**** Potential for GMV growth to reach mid-teens in
FY26 vs the 11.5%-12.5% (FXN) guide, 2) advertising revenue as a percentage of
total GMV to reach 3% from the high 2% range over the last couple quarters, 3)
Commentary around various strategic focus areas including: focus categories,
C2C, eBay Live, and Recommerce, and 4) state of the consumer across its major

  * **MSFT (10/28)****Very much a consensus long and while the buyside expectations for Azure and M365 numbers have understandably increased, Karl Keirstead atleast concludes that the fundamentals support those higher expectations**. Specifically, [Karl believes [analytics.ubs.com]](https://analytics.ubs.com/b/ss/ubsextern-cca-prod/4/REDIR/?v5=Click&v6=SMEP&pe=lnk_o&pev2=link&events=event3&url=https%3A%2F%2Furldefense.com%2Fv3%2F__https%3A%2Fanalytics.ubs.com%2Fb%2Fss%2Fubsextern-cca-prod%2F4%2FREDIR%2F%3Fv5%3DClick%26v6%3DSMEP%26pe%3Dlnk_o%26pev2%3Dlink%26events%3Devent3%26url%3Dhttps*3A*2F*2Fneo.ubs.com*2Fshared*2Fd22ZVF0Ft4%26v2%3D4828%26v3%3D1f1d085062516f80aef03ecfd94c9266*2399*732121768063037%26v4%3Dfalse%26c3%3D1f1d085062516f80aef03ecfd94c9266*2399*732121768063037__%3BJSUlJSV-fn5-%21%21AHh8_Z5O2w%21n2dYBqFpA6RgOKwgVn62CFTzRqa4PgqCAnVBW-4HlVK-c7vBPk1IxzMx4u41RzqeyQ8zZnpnud8r-8rG4zkbCig--BGTEkXLYA%24&v2=4829&v3=1f1d1577bcc16bd0b742ae68c894f631~4095~822640653344600&v4=false&c3=1f1d1577bcc16bd0b742ae68c894f631~4095~822640653344600) the 1Q/Sept Azure bogey is a 2pt beat at 47% growth and investors also inching up their M365 growth estimates on the back of Microsoft’s bigger push to usage-based pricing. That doesn’t screen unreasonable to him especially as his latest enterprise demand checks sounded solid and with OpenAI revs upside likely translating to higher Azure growth, industry AI capacity adds being strong and Microsoft benefiting from hosted GPU inflation. Karl also shares the optimistic view that a faster pivot to usage-based pricing in the Copilot suite as well as greater uptake of Microsoft’s AI security suite could prove to be accretive to M365 growth. In terms of what is driving his Azure expectations: OpenAI upside, GPU, inflation, and capacity adds.

  * **TMUS (10/28)** Wireless sentiment is extremely cautious right now given the latest SPCX developments and what they could ultimately mean for the competitive landscape. With that hanging over the group, it’s hard to know if there’s a print or number that would really be “good enough” to shake those concerns. **Putting the longer-term terminal value debate aside, though, TMUS is still pretty contested.** Bulls point to the strong network, solid service revenue growth and cash generation, with the recent derating leaving room for a relief rally. Bears worry that slowing share gains and a more promotional backdrop mean the historical growth premium is harder to justify. **That said, after all the recent pain in the stock, the bar looks pretty low. Looking purely at the numbers and what’s implied for 2H, the setup hardly feels demanding, especially coming off the first quarter without a beat-and-raise in quite some time.**

  * **AMZN (10/29)****** Very crowded long across both HFs and LOs, but with AWS expectations already pretty high and a long list of boxes that need to be checked for the stock to work, I’m hardly surprised the #1 question I keep getting is the timeless classic: “why does this stock never work?” I’ve heard plenty of answers, but outside of the heavy lab exposure and negative FCF, the two biggest debates into the print seem to be AWS margins and how management addresses the agentic risk. Most investors I talk to are already looking for low-40s AWS growth and margins given how strong cloud checks were intra-quarter, both on pricing and capacity coming online, so anything short of that could weigh on sentiment into YE. On agents, I personally don’t think the competitive risk is as big as investors fear, but it’s clearly a major pressure point, particularly for LOs/generalists. And with 3P data also pointing to some softness in NA retail this quarter, any cautious commentary around Muse/agentic probably gives people one more thing to worry about.

make numerous changes to his estimates - including higher CapEx for 2027 and
beyond. While investor expectations for AWS revenue YOY growth have now caught
up to where Stephen is, where he still diverges vs consensus most meaningfully

believes that investors will be forced to raise margin forecasts as Amazon
reports each successive quarter, driving what should be higher EPS and FCF
forecasts for 2027 and beyond.** And at 18x his updated 2027E EPS, there is
still significant room for the stock to outperform, as Stephen does not

  * **AMZN** **(Buy,** **PT: US$348.00** **Prior: US$318.00)** **\- AWS Margins Are the Next Area of Focus** \- We preview Amazon's 3Q26 results, which it will report on Oct 29. We raise our price target to $348 from $318 as we make numerous changes to our estimates - including higher CapEx for 2027 and beyond. The #1 question we receive on AMZN shares is the lack of follow-through post 2Q26 results. We think this is due to investors pricing in higher CapEx estimates for 2027 (from ~$250B prev. to $300B+) to arrive at zero or negative FCF. While investor expectations for AWS revenue YOY growth have now caught up to where we are, where we still diverge vs consensus most meaningfully is segment operating margin: 46% vs 38% for 2027. The pushback that our margin forecast is too high is straightforward: AI workloads are lower margin. Our answer is equally as straightforward: they cannot spend the revenue dollars fast enough. AWS is set to add an incremental ~$80B of revenue and ~$20B in D&A expenses - hence in order for margin to remain at 2Q26's ~39%, Amazon has to incur ~$29B in incremental SG&A expenses. While this is possible, we argue that it will need to spend at 3x the velocity of what it is set to spend in 2026 on personnel or other items. **Hope everyone had a great weekend.** Loads to get through on the micro side,
so will spare you the long intro, but this update from our PB book was too
interesting not to flag. After hyperscalers became an increasingly popular
source of funds during last week’s selling, **Friday we saw a complete 180**.
HFs fully re-grossed the hyperscaler exposure they had de-risked earlier in
the week, funded by renewed de-grossing across Hardware and Memory. And
honestly, this is becoming quite the pattern: one or two days of aggressive
de-grossing, everyone panics, and then we turn around and buy the whole dip
right back. Wash, rinse, re-gross. Chart below.



![](https://www.ubs.com/emas/CCA/79039d92-a6bb-4e54-8cee-f94f4b4ad0bd/59af4052-e981-45de-a9e1-c881e3157a43.png)



**  MICRO**: **All earnings, all the time this week** , with ~46% of SPY
market cap slated to report, alongside 38% of QQQ and 35% of XLK. Hyperscalers
will, unsurprisingly will take charge, with GOOGL and MSFT Wednesday AMC
followed by AMZN Thursday. Previews are below, and my weekend note from
yesterday has more on some of the other names joining the earnings circus,
notably **AMT, EBAY, TMUS, RBLX, PINS** and more.



**Speaking of earnings, VZ ****first at bat this week and tbh I’m not sure the
numbers matter nearly as much as the qualitative commentary on the call**.
Expect Starlink to be THE focus, especially after all the fun on Friday
following the CNBC podcast. That said, the numbers are solid. PPNA came in at
400K+ versus bogeys in the ~200K range, while FY PPNA guidance was raised to
1.1-1.2M from 750K-1M. Service revenue and EBITDA also came in slightly ahead.
On the softer side, fiber/FWA net adds were a bit light, and we’re already
getting plenty of questions around why the PPNA strength isn’t translating
into a bigger FY revenue raise, with guidance only moving toward the high end.
**So c****ue the never-ending****nitpicks****around****Frontier
led****growth****and****cost-cutting-driven growth.** Guess let’s see what
they said on the 2027 trajectory. On capex, the company reiterated its 2026
outlook, including the “success-based” initiatives (e.g dark fiber). Nothing
on 2027 capex yet, though this has been a huge discussion point given said
dark fiber plans + upcoming spectrum auctions.



Outside of earnings, plenty to chew on from the weekend, with [Elon’s
tweets](https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2114434646914068862?s=43) clearly
winning the award for most cheerful Monday morning reading. **His latest take
on neoclouds was, shall we say, not particularly bullish** : he expects a
“guppy-level death and consolidation,” arguing debt markets have almost
entirely shut off funding for companies without substantial revenue
independent of AI datacenters. _So nothing dramatic, just your standard casual
weekend discussion of industry extinction_. Meanwhile **AMZN** CEO Jassy said
AWS’s 2026 cloud capacity is sold out, most large capacity blocks for 2027 are
already booked and a meaningful share of 2028 is committed. And then there’s
**META , who is officially offering nearly $22.5B in common A stock and $12.5B

subject: JEF Asia morning TMT ideas: Key takeaways from Asia tech group call yesterday. Previews on Yageo and LGD. Global AI bull bear debate call on 28 Oct.
body:
**SELLOFF IN TECH LAST NIGHT SO LOOKING FOR BOTTOM FISH IDEAS??** Conor,
William and Sherman hosted a semis updates and ideas call yesterday which was
well attended with over 500+ investors. Great update by Sherman on his latest
model and our recent data points **more** upside in tech. During the call we
highlight our recent forecasts on TPU / Vera Rubin shipment and most
importantly **CoWoS numbers and top picks within Asia**. Research side, we
also got **previews on Yageo and LGD**. More details below!

**S &P -1.21% / ****DOW +0.02% /****NASDAQ -2.60% / RTY +0.11% / SOX -6.72%
/****WTI +2.21% /****GOLD -2.80% / XBTUSD -3.93% /****VIX +14.09% /****10YY
-2.84%**

Equities sold off sharply, with the S&P suffering its worst day since July, as
funding fears reignited in the AI trade after Meta's results and Lam
Research's in-line guide, with semis leading the move lower. Under the surface
it was risk reduction and rotation rather than panic: the equal-weight S&P
rose, investors piled into Treasuries (10YY fell below 5%), and defensives,
while gold, silver and bitcoin also sold off in a broad deleveraging. Oil
jumped, with Brent at its highest since May (~$113), after the US ordered some
diplomats and families out of Saudi Arabia following Houthi attacks, Trump
said he isn't negotiating and the NYT reported US and Israeli plans for a
short, intensive operation after the midterms, undoing the more constructive
tone of recent days. Another jump in French yields added to the flight to
quality. Earnings outside of tech were generally well received, with PG, CSX,
LMT and BX bid. Staples, ConsDIsc and Utilities led; Tech, Comm Services and
Industrials lagged.

A couple of themes to highlight:

  1. **Thematics:** Volumes better. Breadth constructive despite the headline weakness, with the equal-weight S&P ~190bp better than the SPX. Beta and Growth the standout unperforming Jef baskets with risk-off shift. Defensive sectors saw buying flow on our platform;  
  

  2. **AI Funding – Still the Hottest Topic:** META fell 7.0%, despite a stellar print, as its filing flagged a new non-voting share class and potential need to raise "hundreds of billions”. LRCX (-11.8%) guided in line against a high bar, dragging the SOX -6.7%, with AAPL hovering in the green (+1.2%) was the FCF haven. From this seat , it feels the moves are less about results and more a stark re-evaluation of A as capital markets get more discriminating. Bloomberg’s read is an aggressive de-risking and not a broken cycle, flagging the SOX at the cheapest on forward P/E since March. With no single driver of today’s sell-off, caution appears to be defining sentiment.  
  

  3. **Flight to Quality: Bonds, Builders, Staples:** 10YY fell to 4.95%, back below 5% for the first time in a month; Mortgage rates fell for the first time in nine weeks (7.32%), so homebuilders rallied despite a PHM miss (ITB +5.4%), while staples led the tape (XLP +3.3%) with PG +5.6%, its best day since March 2020 on a broad-based beat. French spreads, which widened to a 15-year high, added to the haven bid, and initial claims of 194K (the lowest since July, per Tom Simons) show the labour market isn't the problem. The next test is the Oct 28 FOMC, where the market prices only ~13% odds of a hike. Would stay with the staples and rate-sensitives while the 10Y holds below 5%.  
  

  4. **Beyond AI – Full Steam Ahead:** CSX (+6.8%) posted a high-quality 3Q beat with operating ratio improving 420bp to 60.9% on 5% volume growth despite soaring diesel, as higher fuel prices push shippers from truck to rail (UNP +3.6%), and LMT (+7.0%) beat and raised on a record backlog. Companies are running ahead of input cost pressure with price hikes and cost cuts, which supports EPS but is net negative for the, with the transport names the conduit for energy into core inflation. Would stay long CSX and the rails. Note [here](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14261063&ad=5043929941&h=9ANP8fF&sig=7LTtGN6SiumvyJVNftXQyGmijbf&v=2&url=https://javatar.bluematrix.com/links2/secure/html/ee930943-88cf-4f21-85bc-966e3a7b77ab).   
  

  5. **Hedge Funds Load Back into Shorts:** Latest GS prime data shows shorts outpacing longs ~5 to 1 this month, with short leverage in the 99th percentile of the past five years, and net leverage among fundamental L/S funds near a three-year low, raising the risk of a sharp squeeze if markets rebound. They note those funds are -2.5% in October (TMT -7.4%), and global IT saw its heaviest two-week net selling in more than a decade of the desk's records through Oct 16.

**** After Hours Earnings: Quick take back with more overnight**

  * **WDC +1% ah****:** Q1 EPS beat, Q1 rev +55% y/y tp $4.38Bn way ahead of street ests. Q2 adj EPS and adj GM guides well above cons, and raised Qtrly div +17% . Stock volatile in the post market as the print hit but sitting higher at time of writing 
  * **NEM +1.22% ah****:**  3Q adj EPS beat, Sales of $6.36Bn inline, Average realized gold price per oz sold $4,317, estimate $4,290. On track to meet full-year 2026 production guidance of 5.3 million attributable gold ounces
  * **DECK -9.71% ah** : raise FY EPS guide, Net sales +3.5% to $1.48Bn y/y but missed cons ests of $1.51Bn.

** **

**ASIA TECH GROUP CALL – WHAT’S NEW FROM CONOR, WILLIAM AND SHERMAN??**



  * **SHERMAN: LATEST VIEW ON TPU/MTK EARNINGS.** Re share px weakness on MTK/TPU related, we believe it was mainly due to expectation mismatch. Some brokers were too bullish on MTK’s m/s within Googl’s in house proj assuming 100% m/s. We reiterate same view. For MTK’s TPU proj: 1) to Anthropic we assume 100% shr by AVGO; 2) for Googl in house we assume MTK holding more shares vs AVGO; while some brokers assume MTK taking 100% causing exp mismatch. Overall, we see no delay in v9 tape out in 1q27 (some bulls exp 4q27 tho) and MP in 1q28. **MTK briefing on 30 Oct.** We exp them to maintain 26-27 ASIC rev guide of 2-2.5bn/16-18bn, respectively.

**![](cid:image001.png@01DD62C3.9B260D90)**

** **

![](cid:image002.png@01DD62C3.9B260D90)

  * **EMIB-T CAPACITY.** 1) end-26: 20k; 2) 27: 40k; 3) 28: 60k. We think the 60k capacity in 2028 would be enough to support 500m v9 production in 2028. Yield is main issue we see only 20-30% for Unimicron; Ibiden/Shinko 40-50%. Our supply chain checks also suggest Trn4 might use EMIB-T.
  * **RUBIN FCTS.** We see some delay due to HBM spec change. We fct vol. of 500-600k in 4q26 vs original 700-800k). And 1q27 of 1-1.2m. This is more related to software side for HBM (not HBM). Rack design not finalized yet perhaps 4q26. NVL288 will not ready in 2027. We see limited vol for 576 in 2027 and exp major ramp in 2028.
  * **MORE ON RUBIN HBM DESPEC & IMPACTS. **2 SKUs now: 1) 192gb for inference and 2) 256gb for training (TBC). That said, we fct HBM px down in 2h27 due to 1) HBM despec; 2) more supply coming in 2027-28; 3) memory makers don’t wanna push asp too high to harm AI demand.
  * **TSM CAPEX.** We exp 86bn in 2027 and 98-100bn in 2028. This is only for TW + Arizona. More upside if we include Texas. Any upsides in 2028 would be related to Texas. We hence fct foundry capex of 150bn in 2027 and 173-175bn in 2028. TSM output hence implied CSP capex of 900bn/1.4-1.5trn/1.8-1.9trn in 2026-28.
  * **ABF SUPER SHORTAGE!** We push ABF names as most shortage among tech verticals given strong agentic AI demand. Conor push for LGI on the back of new client catalysts include AVGO, AWS, MRVL and TSLA. He also like SEMCO on the back of its exposure to AMD + AWS + NVDA, plus potential upside from MU’s BT. ZDT is also our pick given the upcoming HK IPO of their ABF family. We also love AT&S on its dominate shr within mSAP: 800G 40%; 1.6T 100%; 3.2T 100%. ITEQ is our pick in Asia on the back of the CCL shortage theme w 40% shr in AMD and 60% shr in INTC. 5 new supplies coming in for them also helping UTR. Investors love our call tho admitting shrs gone up too much.
  * **MLCC: PX HIKE +VE.** We see to announce across the board px hike in 4q26. Same for Murata.



  * **SEMICAPS: WE PUSH FOR JP NAMES.** US WFE exp were 300bn vs JP 250bn. JP names are yet to raise so could be near term catalysts. We love TEL + Kokusai + Advantest >>> LRCX and AMAT.

** **

**FUBON PREVIEW ON YAGEO.** Joey put out a
[note](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14261063&ad=5043929941&h=4y5bW0y&sig=Va9xMHmJcVYf3uYA4Ok3i2m4SZ&v=2&url=https://javatar.bluematrix.com/links2/secure/pdf/abf78746-7b3b-4558-ae2b-e008f31bc87a).
We believe 3Q26 orders will be as strong as expected, with the B/B ratio
maintained at around 2, UTR of 90%, and the MLCC price increase effect will
drive MLCC sales ratio up to 23%. **We maintain our 3Q26 GM forecast of 39.8%,
and single-quarter EPS forecast of NT$5.61**. Moreover, we believe Japanese
and Korean manufacturers have recently maintained high UTR and B/B ratios, and
have indeed initiated price adjustments for consumer-grade MLCCs, with
adjustments for distributors starting in 3Q26 and for direct customers mostly
beginning in 4Q26. We expect Yageo's 4Q26 orders to remain strong, and the
price increases will continue to be reflected. We forecast 4Q26 sales at
NT$53.7bn, up 8.4% QoQ and 49.3% YoY, GM slightly rising to 41%, and 4Q26 EPS
of NT$6.43. **We reiterate Buy and slightly adjust our target price to NT$812,
representing 25x FY27F EPS.**



KB CUTTING TP for LGD. In Jeff’s
[note](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14261063&ad=5043929941&h=Z_pmYCV&sig=Gpbpb0UkCnK5krEcAviwkoeC9fv&v=2&url=https://javatar.bluematrix.com/links2/secure/pdf/b647e69c-e266-4cbd-99f6-788897199544),
he forecast **3Q26 revenue of KRW6.2tn (+12% QoQ, -10% YoY) and OP at
KRW250.5bn (TTB QoQ, -42% YoY; 4% OPM)**. Despite large-size/mobile OLED
shipments growing on peak seasonality, falling mid-size LCD shipments should
weigh down earnings. In 4Q26, shipment area is expected to rise 10% amid high-
demand seasonality, while ASP per area is projected to climb only 3% due to
weaker PC/smartphone demand and higher memory prices. We forecast 4Q26 OP of
KRW260.6bn (+54% YoY). Looking ahead, we fct 2027 revenue of KRW24tn (-5% YoY)
and OP of KRW745.4bn (+35% YoY). Set makers are expected to assume a
conservative stance on shipment targets to contain cost burdens, while
focusing more on high-end, premium products that allow them to pass on higher
costs more easily. **We maintain BUY on LGD, but cut our TP to KRW10,000.**

**NSCALE**

More -ve headlines on neoclouds…

  * Early Sunday, the Telegraph reported that **MSFT** has recently pulled out of a datacenter deal with UK neocloud **Nscale (private)** (link [here](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14228208&ad=5021965962&h=JDulU58&sig=IyhDOKwl9gOkB1bSLI7IycYxrCQ&v=2&url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2026/10/18/microsoft-axes-ai-deal-setback-uk-data-centre-pioneer/))

    * This is a new datacenter site announced last Sep targeting 50MW (scalable to 90MW), with initially 23,040 GB300’s to be delivered in 1Q27 (link [here](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14228208&ad=5021965962&h=ixhDGKs&sig=FbistziSwxNbPijrraAv9CD0VEY&v=2&url=https://www.nscale.com/press-releases/nscale-uk-ai-infrastructure-announcement))
    * The article does not provide a specific reason on why **MSFT** walked away, but mentions that the site has been contending with a series of delays, and cites power grid officials claiming that they did not expect a power supply for the datacenter until the 2030’s
    * Seems like another datacenter project impacted by power constraints – which is nothing new per se, but won’t be taken +vely in this current market
    * Note also that this UK project is not the only **MSFT** is collaborating with **Nscale** on – others include 1) a 1.35GW site in West Virginia; 2) a >230MW campus in Norway; 3) a broader deal to deploy 200k+ GB300’s across EU and the US 

  * A few hours later, BBG reported that **Nscale** is facing pushback from investors for its IPO valuation of $30bn, with a cohort of investors pushing for a $16-19bn valuation instead (link [here](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14228208&ad=5021965962&h=BJ_QVFn&sig=BYxjgPnuMYIfoLw2oCWMBqQQnWo&v=2&url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-18/ai-cloud-firm-nscale-faces-investor-pushback-over-ipo-valuation))

    * Unclear if the Telegraph article had anything to do with this – but clearly the mood and appetite for neoclouds have taken a turn for the worse since last week…

**AMZN**

Axios with an exclusive interview over the weekend with **AWS** CFO John
Felton (link
[here](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14228208&ad=5021965962&h=OQXM_vs&sig=E2XasyaZvH8M7NL1qE2UQKWY6Ia&v=2&url=https://www.axios.com/2026/10/16/amazon-
web-services-ai-cfo)) – all bullish commentary here, but most interesting to
me was his comment supporting tokenmaxxing for **AWS** , as they are seeing a
“very linear line between productivity and token usage”

  * Felton says he’s “comfortable about what we’re doing” with capex based on a nearly $500 billion order backlog as of Q2, driven by a mix of “big and small customers, large enterprises, large IA labs, but also small and medium-sized businesses”
  * “The demand is real”, and **AWS’** AI server investments are proving fruitful: “We’re seeing paybacks of under three years on those servers.”
  * Some companies have paired back on AI token spending ,putting limits on users to control their costs. But Felton says he studied AWS’ own token usage and found that ,in general, more is better. “What we saw is a very linear line between productivity and token usage,” he says. **AWS** is experiencing “a lot of ROI, a lot of productivity, and we’re planning for more’.”
  * "I've been surprised with some of the anti-data center movement," Felton says. "For me, we're investing in local communities. We are investing to create jobs. I feel like we're doing the right thing." He added that it "does confuse me as to where it's coming from. It makes me feel like we need to get better with our messaging, with what we're doing, why we're doing it, how we're doing it," saying AI companies need to "be much more proactive" and "tell that story, which I think is a very positive story."

**US DATACENTERS**

Our digital infra analyst Jon Petersen has a good report out looking at the
political pressure on DC’s and buildout state by state – clearly this is top
of mind for investors going into midterms – report
[here](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14228208&ad=5021965962&h=aD27LRO&sig=MBwvh8JdCpzViOnbwPyw5SQDxIB&v=2&url=https://javatar.bluematrix.com/links2/secure/html/e3040228-21fd-4c75-85bc-d94bc3a5ff73)

  * Datacenter opposition has gone from 42% to 75% in a year, and it's bipartisan. 9 of the top 15 datacenter states elect governors in Nov, with candidates in both parties backing stricter rules of moratoriums. 
  * But opposition has not materially slowed development, and spend is still running at a record $75bn+ annual pace. Moreover, the ballot box **_changes the cost and location of 2028-30 supply, not the 2026-27 builds already under way_**.
  * About 30GW of his 2028-30 forecast (34% of the total) sits in TX, GA and OH, which we are watching closely on Nov 3
  * In the report, we also go **_state by state through 9 markets: TX, GA, PA, OH, AZ, IL, NV, NY and NM. For each, we look at the governor's race with Polymarket odds, the current rules, where the pipeline sits by stage, and which platforms are exposed_**.

    * TX is the big one at ~22.9GW, or ~26% of 2028-30E deliveries. Abbott is at 78%, and a Hinojosa win would mean an immediate pause.
    * GA is a coin flip at 48/52 on a statewide pause. Probability-weighted, the base case barely moves, though we see the downside scenarios as more plausible than the upside ones.

  * On the trade, he thinks NIMBYism favors the incumbents. **DLR** and **EQIX** get a wider mark-to-market spread on expiring leases, plus decades of experience with local communities that new entrants don't have. Among the HPC developers, approvals are the constraint rather than demand. **RIOT** and **CORZ** have power in hand with nothing pending, and **RIOT** 's Corsicana is the largest uncontracted block in coverage.

**OCP**

Blayne just published his OCP takeaways last Fri – report
[here](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14228208&ad=5021965962&h=pFbuWxL&sig=NBRIFQMqmTQ1jnDZphzhuUyUfAb&v=2&url=https://javatar.bluematrix.com/links2/secure/html/a623f5ac-6024-4dfa-9af2-13cc0a26e345):

  * For scale-out, demand for 1.6T transceivers remain strong, and we continue to forecast 80mn units in 2027 despite concerns of tightness at 3nm – **LITE** and **MTSI** are most levered to this transition
  * For scale-up, the introduction of micro VCSEL arrays could reduce InP laser content required – we view **CRDO** ’s newly released portfolio of ALC’s and Optical Backplane as underappreciated assets, and reiterate the OmniConnect opportunity looks increasingly promising
  * For NPO, we expect it to dominate the scale-up optical design cycle thru 2027-28, given meaningful CPO adoption is pushed out to 2029, with potential of it being pushed further out if NPO deployments are successful – this will drive content uplift opportunity for **MTSI** and **SMTC**
  * **NVDA** ’s USFP announcement, alongside **CSCO** and **ANET** ’s XPO designs that provide paths to 12.8T modules suggest that the pluggables market may be more durable than investors expect
  * Outside optics, the show floor pointed to rising content per server for **LSCC** through split-board designs and the new SCMP standard, and for **RMBS** through 16-channel platforms and MRDIMM, which appeared on roughly half the boards we saw.
  * 800V power was another common theme, and **NVTS** 's collaborations with **NVDA** and MCHP put it in front of customers ahead of the 2027-28 design cycle



**GUC/AVGO**

Rita published some marketing takeaways from her recent marketing trip to
China – report attached.



In the long term, **GUC (3443 TT)** remains her top pick as they look likely
to gain the most share in AI XPU/CPU/auto applications.



But in the short-term, she likes **AVGO** , and think the name looks most
interesting now and is the most undervalued name within ASIC’s:

  * We think investors have significantly underestimated **AVGO** ’s 2028 TPU shipments and largely misunderstood its growth potential. Street chatter that in 2028E **Mediatek** ’s TPU counts more than **AVGO** , which is opposite to our checks. **AVGO** is shipping TPU’s for **GOOGL** internal use and **Anthropic**. As long as **Anthropic** ’s demand remains intact, **AVGO** ’s TPU outlook can’t get worse.
  * Meanwhile, **AVGO** ’s reliance in KU demand outlook for other customers is also strengthening in 2027E-29E – our checks indicate **OAI** has recently increased its demand to **3mn+** units in 2027E (much higher vs our previous assumption of 1mn units), while we also think that **Anthropic** has launched the first ASIC project with **AVGO** , which is expected to tape out in mid-2027E and go to MP in 2H28E.



**GDS**

Follow up note from Edison on **GDS** as he continues to defend the name amid
the US neocloud-dragged selloff – in today’s report, he also has some details
on the **DayOne** IPO and a sensitivity table for **GDS** ’s TP to **DayOne**
’s valuation. But we also conservatively lowered our forecasts to assume some
delay in project timing, and also use a lower our target multiples
(20x->**18x** 2030E EV/EBITDA for **GDS** China, 25x->**23x** 2027E EV/EBITDA
for **DayOne**) to get to our new TP of **$59.6** – report

subject: Worry on Neo-cloud refinancing risk - HY Credit Call Takes - +ve Fundamentals but credit markets tighten, equity is the main remaining lever
body:
Market commentary, not research

  

This is where the credit analysts take centre stage.

  

Jefferies HY Credit analyst Michael Haber is still positive on AI
fundamentals.

  

Michael remains a big AI bull on the underlying economics and adoption, but is
increasingly cautious on access to capital, particularly for the neoclouds.
**_Credit funds are running into AI exposure limits just as unsecured and
convertible financing is becoming harder and more expensive, potentially
constraining neocloud capex and, ultimately, the compute capacity available to
hyperscalers and frontier labs._**

  

The near-term constraints are **tighter capital markets access** and **power-
related execution risk**. As credit channels close, **equity is increasingly
the residual source of financing** , and this is already showing up in price
action ( his full note attached).

  

**1\. Financing Structure and Capital Markets Access**

  * **Funding gap:** First-lien GPU-backed financing usually covers only part of chip-related capex. Generally **10–30% of total capex** has to come from other sources. When the customer is an AI model lab or a non-investment-grade hyperscaler, the portion funded elsewhere can rise toward **~70% of relevant costs** , based on what markets will currently allow.
  * **How companies have filled the gap:**
    * **Customer prepayments** , which reduce cash flows in **years 3–5** of contracts.
    * **Unsecured or convertible debt** raised at the parent level.
    * These businesses are not yet generating free cash flow, so they still need this residual equity-like capital.
  * **Unsecured market:** Unsecured bonds have widened to **12–15%** , which limits further access.
  * **Convert market:** The convert market is smaller than the high-yield market. After backing out equity volatility, converts imply credit spreads **250–350bps wider** than straight unsecured bonds, which are already elevated. Both markets are becoming constrained.
  * **What's left:** With unsecured and convert channels restricted, the remaining options are **short-term debt (STD) markets** and **equity**. Michael said recent equity price action looks consistent with the market recognizing this **loss of credit-market leverage**.



**2\. Fundamentals: Still Positive**

  * Michael remains **bullish on AI and neo-cloud fundamentals**.
  * **Pricing:** D200 rental pricing is higher, and short-term contract pricing is improving:
    * From **~$10mn per MW per year** toward **$15mn per MW per year**.
    * **SpaceX** has signed short-term contracts at **$40–50mn per MW per year** , well above prior levels.
  * **Supply problem, not a demand problem.** ARR has disappointed in some cases, but profitability is improving:
    * Reported **gross margins around 85%**.
    * **Several players have turned positive on operating cash flow.**
    * Unit economics at AI model labs are described as **strong**.
  * **Scale challenge:** The long-term spend is hard for credit markets to underwrite. Cumulative U.S. AI-related spend is cited at **$11.5tn by 2035**.

  

**3\. Data Center / Project Financing Risks**

  * **Past underwriting was too simple:** Earlier data center credits (e.g., **Applied Digital, Wolf, Cipher** and similar) were underwritten mainly on **counterparty risk and completion timing**. Michael comes from energy/power project finance and sees this as too simple for large, long-duration projects with heavy regulatory and permitting complexity.
  * **Power permitting is the most important underwriting factor:**
    * Some large U.S. hyperscaler projects are going ahead with data center construction **without secured power permissions**.
    * Tenants, including hyperscalers, are reluctant to proceed without a clear path to power delivery. This creates **walk-away risk**.
  * **Data center credit primer:** A recent primer on data center credit (focused on **powered shells**) ranks **~10 factors** relevant to principal protection. **Power permitting is ranked among the highest.**



**4\. Implications for Equity Markets**

  * **Shift in financing channels:** Losing economic access to unsecured and convert markets means more reliance on equity issuance. This supports the view that volatility and pressure in neo-cloud and AI infrastructure stocks partly reflect **higher expected dilution** , or the need to raise equity on worse terms.
  * **Pricing power from tight supply:** Higher rental rates and contract pricing, including very high short-term rates, are good for revenue and margin trajectories if companies can secure **capital and power**. This favors names with **contracted power, near-term capacity or more balance-sheet flexibility**.
  * **Execution and permitting risk:** Power permitting delays or failures can hurt project economics, delay cash-flow conversion and **force additional capital raises**. Equity investors should prefer companies with **secured power, advanced permitting or diversified financing sources**. They should be more cautious on **pure development-stage or unsecured-dependent stories**.
  * **Duration and scale:** Credit markets alone will struggle to fund a multi-year, multi-trillion-dollar capex path, so equity remains the residual capital provider. Near term, equity performance is likely to respond more to **financing updates, contract pricing announcements and power-related milestones** than to demand narratives alone.

Michael is **positive on AI/neo-cloud unit economics and rental pricing** but
**cautious on the financing and power-execution path**. Once credit markets
tighten, **equity is the main remaining lever** , and that is already
affecting price action. The debate is moving from _" Is AI demand real?"_ to
**_" Who can finance and power the buildout?"_**

**_  
_**

Happy to discuss further or set up a follow-up call with Michael.

**ANTHROPIC**

With the whole market seemingly holding its breath into the Investor Day,
**Anthropic (private)** basically whiffed – no updated ARR # was officially
given, and the main disclosures we got (at least what has been reported
publicly so far) were 1) 3Q revs of $16.8bn (+45% q-q, decel vs 2Q’s +104%);
2) 3Q adj. GPM of 85%; 3) 3Q adj. OPM of 11%+ (link
[here](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14208362&ad=5007462929&h=_Dt7Wtu&sig=QVUumOC4T4ifxMz5gmoKyF1GcZU&v=2&url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-14/anthropic-
revenue-jumps-to-16-8-billion-in-quarter-before-ipo)).



The implied ARR here is likely not ~$67bn ($16.8bn x 4), but more closer to
$70-76bn (depending on your assumption for Aug/Sep). Regardless, this is still
well below the so-called end-Sep bogeys of ~$80bn, and also implies Aug/Sep
revs coming in mostly flattish (see the below chart from TickerTrends, link
[here](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14208362&ad=5007462929&h=dsmb7E2&sig=J3wy3pTHlwhSURE6nNEaFTFnrfy&v=2&url=https://blog.tickertrends.io/p/anthropics-q3-revenue-
growth-slowed)).



Also worth noting that in this Reuters article overnight (link
[here](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14208362&ad=5007462929&h=mwpWm4c&sig=M9H4QzlfW6NWQWiNkvshCZIhZEa&v=2&url=https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/anthropics-q3-revenue-
surges-45-nearly-17-billion-2026-10-14/)), where they talked about a $110bn
ARR by end-2026E (originally they said it was from “another person who
attended the event”, but have changed the source now to “analysts who met with
company ‌executives earlier ⁠this week” – and the Reuters reporter clarified
on X that this was indeed NOT something directly disclosed by the company
yesterday, link
[here](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14208362&ad=5007462929&h=pxcd_8s&sig=5Bpv2tvmNqEoGSkpe08IGFvaWWW&v=2&url=https://x.com/readkrystalhu/status/2110591277964394971?s%3D20)).

![Image](cid:image007.jpg@01DD5C22.B249B000)



Nonetheless, a miss is a miss – arguably there are some nuances with the 3Q
#’s (likely some -ve impacts from the distillation cut and **META/MSFT**
churning, and Opus 5.5 only launched in late-Sep so Oct should reaccel), and
some also argue that this is just reflective of **Anthropic** losing share to
**OAI** , and thus does not necessarily mean the AI labs are no longer growing
(one should look at **Anthropic** +**OAI** combined growth) – but clearly the
market does not have the patience for nuance now, and investors were generally
hoping for some form of reassurance from this event – something that we
clearly did not get.



The bigger issue here is how myopically focused the entire market is on a
single wonky metric from a private company, that only gets reported by media
outlets and/or 3P data source, each with their own interpretations – I’m sure
everyone (including myself) are sick and tired of this by now. And so by that
logic, when (if?) **Anthropic** actually goes public, the public disclosure
should help reduce some of this uncertainty.



Question is, where do we go from here, with sentiment now taking another leg
down? Unfortunately, it does feel like everything in the near-term will still
be determined by further updates with this **Anthropic** IPO (Timing still
mid-Nov? Valuation still $2trn? Any potential incrementals to look for in the
S-1 filing?), and tough to see investors jumping in to catch the falling knife
here or massively regross on AI names before the listing actually happens.
From my seat in the past few weeks, get the sense that _investors have been
increasingly turning more -ve and defensive_ , and the _convos have been
around selling YTD winners, shorting the crowded longs, rotating to lower beta
AI names_ (e.g., hyperscalers, **NVDA, TSM, ASML**), and _diversifying into
non-AI names_ (**AAPL** or software/internet within TMT, or other sectors like
healthcare, financials).

**US HYPERSCALERS PREVIEW**

Brent published his 3Q previews for the US hyperscalers + **CRWV** – report

Detailed 75 page slide deck inside which includes takes from our proprietary
ad survey. Reminder that the team is hosting a call later today at 1030am ET
to discuss their views– register
[here](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14208362&ad=5007462929&h=GSiTrSN&sig=UEsdpV9Ukc52TTcTGQeNyHZ27jb&v=2&url=https://jefferies.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_IeO7v_JGQC2kfh_7Tar0tA).



  * Cloud checks remain bullish, with demand outpacing supply & pricing moving higher across hyperscalers & neoclouds. As incremental capacity comes online, strong monetization should support further growth accel, resilient mgns & cont. reinvestments. 
  * In total, we model CY26 capex for hyperscalers + **ORCL** \+ **META** to ~$818B (+84% y-y), and CY27 capex of ~$1.17trn (+43% y-y), with upside risk as the buildout continues. 
  * On ads, near-term trends remain resilient despite consumer pressure, with **AMZN, META** and **GOOGL** screening most positively. Our proprietary ad survey suggests agent adoption & its potential impact on ad spend remains early, though personal agents like Muse could reshape where dollars flow over time
  * **MSFT**

    * We think the Sep-Q Azure bogey is at **~47% y-y cc** (vs street’s +45%), while M365 Comm should also accelerate to 17% y-y as Copilot drives ARPU expansion
    * Margin compression also has come in better than expected, despite elevated AI investments
    * Despite the post-2Q earnings outperformance vs peers (+39% vs **META/AMZN/GOOGL** +30%/+10%/+3%), we believe **MSFT** ’s momentum can continue
    * Stock currently trades at ~26x NTM P/E vs its 5-yr avg of 28x
    * We raise our TP from $575->**$650** (based on 28x FY28E)

  * **GOOGL**

    * We think the 3Q cloud bogey is at **100%+ y-y** (vs street’s +90%), with wildcard upside from 3P TPU sales (though bigger inflection not till 2027E), and Gemini 4 has brought **GOOGL** back closer to frontier model performance 
    * For Search, we think bogeys are at **~13.5% y-y** (vs street’s +15%), and while there are some questions on sustainability of strong Search ad revs given the tough 2H comps, checks indicate **GOOGL** remains the dominant channel for advertisers, and we expect the company to make the pivot to consumer agents by leveraging its huge stack.
    * Stock currently trades at ~15x EV/EBITDA vs its peak of ~20x

  * **META**

    * We expect a modest beat for 3Q revs (**+23.7% y-y** vs street’s +23.5%) and 4Q revs (+24.1% y-y vs street’s +22.9%), given conservative estimates vs pre-COVID seasonality
    * Our ad survey supports **META** 's positioning to capture incremental ad spend in 2H
    * We also expect upside to FY26 capex estimates, and potential qualitative FY27 capex guidance, given the firm’s growing compute needs, as well as +ve commentary on Muse and other AI offerings
    * We think there is still more room for the stock run, given the growing AI momentum and favorable backdrop into the holiday season

  * **AMZN**

    * We think the 3Q **AWS** bogey is now at **40%+ y-y** (vs street’s +37%)
    * Retail has continued to surprise +vely despite cautious consumer sentiment
    * While future capex spend is biased upward and pressures cash flows, backlog is growing faster (2Q +154% y-y), which combined with relatively quick payback + Cloud pricing power, reduces concerns on capex loads
    * Stock currently trades at NTM EV/EBITDA 11x, a 4x/8x discount vs **GOOGL/WMT**

  * **CRWV******

    * We expect a strong 3Q margin beat vs street’s 6.9%, driven by higher GPU pricing and continued execution on their DC buildout, as well more upside to RPO backlog ($130bn+ vs 2Q’s $104bn)
    * Stock trading at 9x fwd EV/EBIT, much cheaper vs NBIS at 47x despite CRWV expected to be have >2x higher margins by end-2028E

**GOOGL**

Brent also has a separate note on specifically on **GOOGL** where he still
defends the name as one of his top picks – report
[here](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14208362&ad=5007462929&h=hW6XJFK&sig=CNZ4rWzIk8Vbwmu1SPT9VKWZbw&v=2&url=https://javatar.bluematrix.com/links2/secure/html/30ba9e54-3e74-4620-b7a1-c1393ab80615).
Detailed 60+ page slide deck in there, here are the key points of argument:

  * **Gemini does not need to be #1 to win** – as models leapfrog each other and commoditize, the advantage shifts from benchmarks to the harness, where **GOOGL** excels with unmatched distribution (5 apps with 3B+ users), data (Googlebot sees 4.8x more of the web than MSFT) and infrastructure. Gemini's price-performance and world-class research talent supercharge that vertically integrated stack, and we view a competitive Gemini as a winning Gemini.
  * **Capex is backed by committed demand** – incremental backlog adds are 3x capex over the past ~2 yrs, with >50% of backlog expected to convert to revenue within 24 months, providing strong visibility into returns. Early evidence is already showing, as Cloud margins nearly doubled to ~36% in a yr even as capex kept rising, while OCF can fund nearly all of capex. NT FCF pressure is real, but the path to ROI is clear, with AI server paybacks of <2 yrs (and even better for TPU’s at half that) vs ~2-3 yrs at **AMZN**.
  * **GCP is winning more than its fair share** – boosted by Gemini, GCP has accelerated for 5 straight quarters at the steepest rate among peers and is on track to gain ~5pp share from CY24 to CY26E. Enterprise AI is now Cloud's primary growth driver (~90% of the F100 use Gemini Enterprise), while TPUs add both a cost edge and a new external revenue stream. With demand outpacing capacity, we expect more share gains as new capacity comes online.
  * **Agentic commerce changes discovery, not GOOGL's relevance** – we've seen this movie before, as **GOOGL** answered chatbots with AI Overviews & AI Mode, both scaling to 1bn+ MAUs at record pace. **GOOGL** has every ingredient agents need, from intent to merchant data to compute, & still leads on ad conversion. We think ad dollars will shift formats rather than leave, & **GOOGL** owns many of the surfaces where AI monetization will happen.
  * **Valuation remains compelling –****GOOGL** trades at 23x CY27 P/E, roughly in line w/ other megacaps & 15x NTM EV/EBITDA, below its 20x peak. We think continued AI execution, Cloud share gains & Search durability can close that gap. We believe its superior fundamentals & diversified portfolio warrant a premium

**MEDIATEK**

Sherman slightly revises up his #’s for **Mediatek (2454 TT)** after better-
than-expected 3Q revs – report
[here](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14208362&ad=5007462929&h=LkCTJZx&sig=Tz1h9NsUjhIi5cEE7DGaQivr0TB&v=2&url=https://javatar.bluematrix.com/links2/secure/pdf/6bc08e03-8972-4aab-9fd5-f82d56404eb5).
Some notable incremental updates to his view in the report (_and_ _pls ping
for a copy of his ASIC and EMIB worksheet_):

  * ASIC

    * He admits that market expectations are a bit too high now, with some investors expecting **Mediatek** to take 100% share in TPU V9, and for them to win V10 as well
    * Sherman forecasts **Mediatek** will likely ship 3.54mn/4.5mn TPU units in 2027E/28E, which implies ~60% share for **GOOGL** ’s in-house TPU demand – but we also need to consider the TPU’s sold to **Anthropic** , which will likely still be all done by **AVGO** – so if including that, **Mediatek** ’s share of total TPU’s will likely be closer to ~40%. See the charts below
    * We forecast **Mediatek** ’s ASIC revs at US$2.2bn/US$16.5bn/US$58.5bn for 2026E/27E/28E, with GPM of 38-39%
    * **SPCX** as a 2nd ASIC customer could provide further upside in late-2028E (we model for potential US$1.8bn/US$7.2bn/US$13.7bn rev contribution in 2028E/29E/30E), though this is not yet confirmed

  * EMIB

    * Sherman’s new EMIB worksheet assumes usable capacity of **20k/40k/60k** per month by end-2026E/27E/28E, with an avg capacity of **50k** in 2028E
    * Assuming 70% V9 allocation, 100% utilization, 16 package positions per EMIB, and 80% assembly yield, our modeled 2028E output reaches **5.4mn** good packages, which covers our 3.6mn TPU V9 forecast by 1.5x. But if we assume a lower 80% utilization and 70% yield, the output would fall to 3.8mn, leaving only a 5.5% buffer. 
    * Allocation is not a contracted entitlement; substrate, logic/HBM supply, and qualification remain critical. 
    * Besides TPU’s, our checks suggest that **AWS** is currently considering using EMIB, which makes Intel’s EMIB supply more promising entering 2028E. 
    * Given the currently still-low production yield, we think **INTC** ’s strategy is to become more aggressive in building capacities including funding its substrate partners, such as **Unimicron (3037 TT), Ibiden (4062 JP)** and others.

ultimately drives our 2027E/28E EPS +7%/+12% higher to €60.77/€71.23. But we
still expect a derating to low-20’s multiple (vs 25x currently), fueled by
market skepticism on the lofty 2028E/29E #’s – and this skepticism is unlikely
to go away, given rising concerns about Chinese competition on DRAM,
datacenter power availability, and financing.



For 2028E, we now model for **109** low-NA EUV systems, **8** high-NA systems,
and **180** immersion systems – but we only model for flattish y-y margins, as
we remain concerned that industry supply tightness could ease by then, and the
400bps+ of margin upside from software upgrade sales could start to reverse.



**SHOP**

Samad publishes his 3Q preview for **SHOP** – stock has been a strong
performer and now hovering around 52-week highs. But we expect the momentum to
continue, with +ve 3P data suggesting upside to 3Q GMV (we forecast **+31%
y-y**), and the setup for 4Q remains reasonable (GMV/rev bar of +28%/+30%
y-y). Report is
[here](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14208362&ad=5007462929&h=1LT18Ef&sig=SVFxfUrlXqrnrw0469MRTRMlxGg&v=2&url=https://javatar.bluematrix.com/links2/secure/html/8c8b12cd-4c55-4bd7-8895-b2e97c408720)



Investor feedback suggests that while fundamentals matter (stock is priced for
25%+ GP$ growth through 2027E), it likely matters less vs the potential impact
from Muse and other personal AI assistants:

  * Investors currently view the broad diffusion of a personal AI assistant into the hands of consumers as bullish, as more commerce will shift online and enterprise merchants will be forced to modernize, and both outcomes would benefit **SHOP**. 
  * But concerns still linger on the potential threat of **META** capturing some value of the checkout layer via its newly announced Meta Pay – though we think the near-term risk is likely overstated as **SHOP** and **META** have explicitly partnered to enable Shop Pay checkout within Muse, and **SHOP** 's payments business is somewhat protected by its pricing structure for 3P processors. 
  * While we acknowledge the long-term risk that **META** seeks to capture some payments economics, we see Muse as a positive validation of **SHOP** ’s agentic commerce positioning, with incremental AI-driven GMV likely more important than potential payments share leakage in the near-term.

**_Macro + Movers._**



Nasdaq futures down 100bps while S&P 500 futures are down 20bps as of writing.



Recall yesterday on our desk, **Tech had the largest sell skew since the day
before the SA portfolio was bought** , the flow chart further below is across
all client types. Net skew was 2.6σ for sale, a historically elevated level.



On the macro front, 10-year yields continue to pull in dramatically and are
now sitting at ~1-month lows and ~25-30bps off the highs. **We think this is
largely a function around the sentiment in AI**.



In European trading, Semis / DC linked names notably lower (SU.FP, IFX.GY,
ASML), while ERIC is up 10% post a stronger organic revenue # and SAP is
higher heading into earnings next week.



Also worth calling out the strength in India this AM, a largely anti-AI
levered market vs. something like the KOSPI, and names like INFO.IN are up
~200bps overnight.



In the US, lower beta / defensive / crowded shorts are outperforming early
(AAPL, PAYX, HUBS, etc) with the flip side of that is u/p.



Busy day on the macro front. But where we sit in the tape and watching the
move in rates even in the face of hotter CPI data yesterday, **it feels like
PPI and Retail sales will take a back seat to the AI trade today in terms of
the direction of the markets**.

**_Anthropic Takes._**



The big story of last night, **and really the reason for a tremendous amount
of market angst in the last several sessions, was the anticipation and fear
around Anthropic’s updated #’s**.



*ANTHROPIC REVENUE JUMPS TO $16.8B IN THIRD QUARTER BEFORE IPO

*ANTHROPIC TOLD INVESTORS WAS PROFITABLE ON ADJUSTED BASIS: FT



As far as everything we’ve read and heard as of right now right now, we never
ultimately got an official Sept. ending ARR metric last night. That being
said, still lots of discussions and trying to bridge the gap between revenue
and ARR, which requires a lot of assumptions.



The other discussions that are increasingly **coming up right now is
assumptions around distillation % of revenue, customer concentration via MSFT
and META** , and then arguably one of the more important dynamics just given
the non-GAAP data is the definitions. Ultimately, it feels like folks are
shaking out that Sept. ARR is < $80B and closer to the ~$75B range.



To state the obvious, we**think everyone will be very happy when we finally at
least one of these labs in the public domain and we can look at real
financials**.



There was also a story going around late last night from
[Reuters](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14207884&ad=5007147590&h=mwpWm4c&sig=XubvTlYY0SSrjko8OE3ITFYZdaN&v=2&url=https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/anthropics-q3-revenue-
surges-45-nearly-17-billion-2026-10-14/) discussing a $110B EOY ARR metric,
**some clarification from that reporter below**.

**_Hyperscaler Preview._**



Brent’s out with his
[previews](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14207884&ad=5007147590&h=FVlhWqs&sig=MFl5kS9V0PtWsQLg9ENSZj86Xrr&v=2&url=https://javatar.bluematrix.com/links2/secure/html/91889b40-b6cc-4424-99f7-1945fd12651a)
into the Cloud earnings over the next few weeks **favoring MSFT (Azure &
M365/Copilot acceleration) and GOOGL (Cloud growth could hit triple digits;
looming TPU upside; 5-pt valuation pullback)**, while also highlighting CRWV
(RPO upside, recognized as best Neo).



He also notes cloud checks remain bullish, w/ demand outpacing supply &
pricing moving higher across hyperscalers & neoclouds. **As incremental
capacity comes online, strong monetization should support further growth
accel, resilient mgns & cont. reinvestments**.



**A few quick 1-liners on the names** :



  * **MSFT****:** F1Q27 sets up well with **Azure & M365 accelerating and valuation still compelling**. Azure’s 44-45% CC guide leaves room for upside as AI demand continues to outstrip supply and pricing remains strong, while M365 Commercial should accelerate.
  *  
  * **GOOGL****:** Cloud accel should trump Search Ad decel. Valuation has retreated to more reasonable levels (~15x EV/EBITDA vs. ~20x peak), Cloud is accelerating with wildcard upside from 3P TPU sales, **and Gemini 4 has brought GOOGL back closer to frontier model performance**. 



  * **META****:** Conservative ests. for 3Q/4Q rev leave upside on the table amid positive ad checks. Brent expects a modest 3Q rev beat & upside to 4Q guide given conservative ests. 



  * **AMZN****:** Accelerating AWS, resilient retail, & discounted valuation. **AWS is not yet done accelerating and AMZN ecom/retail has continued to surprise positively despite cautious consumer sentiment**. 



  * **CRWV****:** Expect **strong margin beat w/ potential RPO backlog upside driven by persistent supply-demand imbalance**. CRWV's CRO noted that exciting announcements are coming regarding mgns during its Fully Connected Conference, & that along w/ higher GPU pricing & continued execution support upside to current ests.



\- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

**_GOOGL Deep Dive._**



Brent’s out with a [deep
dive](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14207884&ad=5007147590&h=-tfxCXa&sig=6oj1pjpeG3OJdlDL1wOyiPKOXQD&v=2&url=https://javatar.bluematrix.com/links2/secure/html/2623743f-0011-4a49-bed2-856d42e787c3)
on GOOGL **where he keeps his buy and leaves his #’s unchanged** with a $445
PT, but examines the different parts of the business.



He notes that the r/r remains favorable, & **he believes the stock can grind
back to its 20x peak from 15x NTM EV/EBITDA now,** driven by a data &
distribution moat that lets Gemini win w/o being #1, AI ROI backing capex; GCP
share gains w/ TPUs a new rev stream; **and personal AI shifting ad formats,
not GOOGL's relevance**.

**_NFLX Transfer Coverage._**



**Jefferies is shifting lead coverage of NFLX to John Colantuoni and
maintaining a Buy rating**. He sees monetization upside, scale-driven margin
expansion, and share repurchases combining for 10 yrs of 14%+ EPS growth. In
addition, **he sees increased visibility on capital allocation and engagement
trends creating a favorable setup in 2027** , helping drive multiple
appreciation from currently depressed levels as focus shifts back to NFLX's
attractive EPS algorithm.

**_Other Jefferies Research._**



**SHOP Preview** : Samad
[expects](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14207884&ad=5007147590&h=SA8uMwN&sig=OzLmj0hhggXtfjXF7gFEFtOs761&v=2&url=https://javatar.bluematrix.com/links2/secure/html/1d50c00d-42c1-4e29-89b0-8af56ac503f9)
another strong print in 3Q, with positive 3P data suggesting GMV upside, and a
reasonable setup for 4Q. **Investor feedback suggests fundamentals matter (the
stock is priced for 25%+ GP$ growth through 2027)** , but less than the
positive/negative disruption posed by broad consumer adoption of Personal AI
assistants. While the stock has rallied ahead of results, a strong print
paired with clarity on the relationship with Muse can push shares higher.



**SAIL Demos** : Gallo
[attended](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14207884&ad=5007147590&h=1R-IBCQ&sig=bR01RFVfYfJOPcm9Q4m9F7bd1K&v=2&url=https://javatar.bluematrix.com/links2/secure/html/6c8339d4-41a1-40e9-b09d-56eaefb6ba88)
SAIL's prod recap demo, which provided incremental prod color & reinforced
SAIL's agentic differentiation. While messaging was consistent with last
week's Navigate conf & our NDR, **he walked away more positive on SAIL's role
in an inflecting agentic identity market**. Separately, **ACN noted at its
investor day that its agentic commerce pipeline grew from 0 in Jan to $1B,
providing another sign that agent adoption (albeit consumer) is beginning to

**_ASML_**** _earnings:_**_Desk View:_ I think these are solid results.
Feedback from investors was that you were unlikely to get a real 2027 unit
increase (up to 90 units at best) so I don’t think it is a real negative that
you didn’t get an update to those numbers but also hard to get the stock to
really work on the print without an increase to that. I think stronger margins
(which is increasingly important when investors are so high on WFE over the
next few years already) and demand commentary into 2030 are incremental
positives on the print and I think small positives are the best bulls could
realistically ask for on the print. So overall slight positive, but nothing
really that thesis changing in the numbers.

**_ _**

_Simon Coles on ASML earnings
([link](https://barclays.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14198989&ad=5001216180&h=y-nIQ9S&sig=MhADA9033HOdA0OVACJWOiaRYO9&v=2&url=https://live.barcap.com/go/publications/link?contentPubID%3DFC6acf17d68ce262721038b8b0)),
_“The two key debates in our view heading in were pricing and expanding
capacity further. ASML has completed pricing negotiations which should benefit
2027 and fully imapct 2028. On capacity, ASML is indicating that demand is so
strong its current plans to increase capacity 30% in 2027 and 2028 are not
enough and thus it is exploring routes to expand further. ASML indicates that
short and medium term demand is increasing all the time. It has received a lot
of orders for 2028 and even seeing strong interest already to place orders for
2029 and sometimes even 2030. We estimated the backlog could be €55bn+ (see
[here(open in new
tab)](https://barclays.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=14198989&ad=5001216180&h=o5T0eIF&sig=4b0v47e2vxKBf4PBDwR13lyTEps&v=2&url=https://live.barcap.com/go/publications/link?contentPubID%3DFC6ac44dd4279c3f3c898fcc32))
which now looks conservative. We think bulls were looking for further upside
to 2027 (90-100 EUV units) but that will have to wait for January which we
expect to be another positive update. The quarter itself is in line on
revenues but well ahead at the margin and EPS level due to strong installed
base management revenues and one-off help from the revaluation of Mistral AI.”
